Definition: from G2930; to make (i.e. intransitively, resemble) ice ("crystallize"):--be clear as crystal.
BiblicalUsage: Clear as crystal appears once, in the description of the New Jerusalem in Revelation 21:11: her light was like a stone most precious, "clear as crystal." The word is the verb for what crystal does — it shines through, with nothing hidden or clouded.
TheologicalSignificance: What convinces me here is that this city is described that way for a reason: in the end, everything will be clear, and the light will pass through without a shadow.
